*Module 3 - Drug Management*

Cross-cutting drug management indicators across all four PC-NTDs. Tablets received vs provided tracks distribution efficiency. Drug loss and wastage trends flag supply chain issues requiring investigation. Drug request vs approved shows whether national procurement requests are being fully met by donors via the JRSM process.
SPACER_ITEM_FOR_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT_CONVENIENCE
SPACER_ITEM_FOR_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT_CONVENIENCE

*Module 2 - Treatment Pipeline*

The treatment pipeline tracks population flow from endemicity through targeting, treatment, and non-treatment. Gaps between population requiring PC and population targeted indicate under- or over-targeting relative to endemicity requirements. Currently shows LF.

*SL NTD National Dashboard*

National-level overview of NTD programme performance across five diseases: 
- Lymphatic Filariasis (LF)
- Onchocerciasis (Oncho)
- Schistosomiasis (SCH)
- Soil-Transmitted Helminths (STH)
- Trachoma.

Use the disease-specific dashboards (3–7) for deeper programme analysis. This dashboard is intended for national programme managers and M&E officers tracking cross-cutting trends.

*Module 1 - Coverage Overview*

WHO therapeutic coverage target for all PC-NTDs is 80% of the targeted population. Coverage Gap shows the percentage-point shortfall from full coverage — a negative gap indicates a denominator data quality issue stale or undersized targeted population) rather than genuine over-treatment.

*Module 2 - Coverage by District*

District-level coverage rate for the most recent reporting year alongside the 10-year trend per district. High variance between districts in the trend chart indicates inconsistent programme implementation or data quality issues at district level — both warrant investigation before attributing to true coverage differences.

*SL NTD District Dashboard*

District-level performance across Sierra Leone's 13 districts. Use this dashboard to identify geographic disparities in coverage, flag districts requiring targeted programme support, and compare district performance over time. Currently showing LF and cross-cutting NTD indicators — disease-specific district breakdowns are available in dashboards 3–6.

*Module 1 - District Performance Overview*

The District Performance Pivot provides a single-view summary of coverage across all districts for the most recent year. Use this as the entry point for identifying which districts are below the 80% WHO coverage target and require follow-up. The scorecard below provides a ranked view with traffic-light formatting.

*Module 1 - National Overview*

- Total Persons Treated — total individuals who received LF treatment nationally
- Therapeutic Coverage % — proportion of targeted population treated (target: 80%)
- Coverage vs Refusal Rate — tracks coverage trend against refusal rate over time
- Treated vs Targeted vs Required — compares actual treatment against programme targets
- Treatment Gap — population treated vs still untreated each year
- Therapeutic Coverage Map — district-level coverage distribution

*Module 2 - District Breakdown*
 
- Coverage Rate by District — compares treatment coverage across all 13 districts
- Population Treated by District — absolute numbers treated per district
- District Coverage Scorecard — coverage, refusal, and gap rates with performance legend
- Treatment Trend by District — multi-year treatment trajectory per district

- Endemicity Status by District — classification of LF endemicity per district
- Target Population by Age Group — breakdown of Pre-SAC, SAC, and Adult targets over time
- Endemicity Status by District — classification of LF endemicity per district

*Module 5 - Drug Management & Adverse Events*
 
- Drug Management by District — tablets received, used, and remaining per district
- Adverse Events by District — serious adverse events reported per district
- Adverse Events Trend — national trend of adverse events and referrals over time
For the other disease states (oncho, SCH, STH), the drug visualizations can use the same visualizations, but will need period changed as per the month the given MDA is performed.

*Module 4 - Treatment by Age and Sex*

MDA coverage disaggregated by age group and sex allows equity analysis across the programme — identifying whether Pre-SAC, SAC, and Adult populations are being reached proportionally, and whether male and female populations show consistent coverage patterns. WHO's therapeutic coverage targets apply across all age groups; persistent gaps in any single band indicate a targeting or mobilisation issue specific to that population segment.

Pre-SAC (children under 5) and SAC (children 5–14) are the highest-burden age groups for most PC-NTDs and typically the primary focus of MDA targeting. Adult coverage is critical for LF specifically, where adult transmission sustains endemicity even when child coverage is high.

*Module 1 - National MDA Overview*

Trachoma MDA uses oral Azithromycin as the primary treatment. Coverage target is 80% of the targeted population. Treatment mix across drug types reflects disease severity and patient age. Refusal rates above 10% indicate community engagement gaps.

Note: Trachoma data is reported at national level only.  District-level disaggregation is not available in the current programme reporting structure.

*Module 2 - Trichiasis (TT) Management*

Trichiasis (inturned eyelashes) is the blinding stage of trachoma requiring surgical intervention. Surgery is the gold standard treatment — high epilation proportions may indicate surgery access barriers. WHO elimination requires TT prevalence below 0.1% in adults 15+.

*Module 3 - Child MDA*

Child MDA targets children aged 6 months to 9.9 years, administered approximately 4 weeks after the main community MDA. This age group carries the highest active infection burden and is the primary reservoir for trachoma transmission.

*Module 4 - Elimination Indicators*

WHO elimination thresholds: TF (Trachomatous Inflammation - Follicular) below 5% in children aged 1–9 years triggers eligibility for impact survey. TT (Trichiasis) below 0.1% in adults 15+ confirms elimination of TT as a public health problem. Both must be met for elimination declaration.

*Module 5 - Drug Management*

Azithromycin is donated through the International Trachoma Initiative (ITI). Drug utilisation efficiency is tracked via the gap between tablets received and provided to clients. Rising wastage or loss trends warrant supply chain review.

*Trachoma WASH Indicators*

The F (Facial cleanliness) and E (Environmental improvement) components of the SAFE strategy address trachoma transmission pathways. Trachoma spreads via eye-seeking flies attracted to ocular and nasal discharge — reduced by improved water access, sanitation, and handwashing practices. WASH improvements sustain elimination after MDA rounds are completed and prevent reinfection.


---

*Water Access*
Households within 30 minutes of a water source face lower barriers to facial washing. Households with water in the compound have the lowest transmission risk. High proportions travelling over 1 hour indicate elevated trachoma transmission risk areas requiring targeted WASH intervention.

---

*Sanitation*
Open defecation is the primary driver of fly breeding and trachoma transmission through the E component of SAFE. Rising private latrine coverage and falling open defecation rates are the key progress indicators. Shared latrines provide partial protection but are less effective than private facilities.

---

*Handwashing*
Facial cleanliness requires both a handwashing facility and availability of soap and water. A facility without soap or water provides limited protection. Track facility presence, soap availability, and water availability together for a complete picture of F component progress.
